detailed_rationale:
Avanti Feeds is India's largest shrimp-feed producer (joint venture with Thailand's Thai Union) and also processes/exports frozen shrimp, chiefly to the US. The quant scorecard flags this as a Sell on the 1-year axis specifically (final_score_1y 35.96, recommendation_1y Sell), driven by a weak 1-year growth score (34.4/100) and recent stage-timing weakness, even though the 3-year axis is a comfortable Hold (final_score_3y 54.7). Digging into why: the sector spent much of the past year under a severe, near-existential overhang — a 50% US reciprocal tariff on Indian shrimp exports, versus a far lower rate (around 15%) for competitor Ecuador — which would have made Indian shrimp structurally uncompetitive in its largest export market and plausibly explains both the weak recent revenue growth and the poor recent stock performance that the quant model is picking up.

The critical, dated fact this research surfaced is that the US reciprocal tariff on Indian goods (including shrimp) was cut from 50% to 18%, effective February 2, 2026 — a major de-risking event that came after the period the trailing 1-year growth/momentum data would have captured, alongside the conclusion of the India-EU FTA and India-UK CETA, both of which further diversify export market access. FY26 results already show the business stabilizing on this basis: consolidated revenue grew 8.3% to Rs 6,066 crore and net profit rose to Rs 656.8 crore (from Rs 557.1 crore), processed shrimp exports grew 20%, and operating margin expanded to 12%. Management's FY27 targets (5.8 lakh MT feed sales, 10-12% export volume growth, flat-to-slightly-improved production) describe a business normalizing rather than one in structural decline.

Given that the tariff cut is a genuine, verifiable, and very recent catalyst that materially changes the forward competitive picture versus what trailing 12-month data would suggest, and that FY26 results already show real (if modest) growth and margin recovery, I judge the quant Sell signal to be capturing stale tariff-crisis-era weakness rather than the current, improved reality.
recommendation_rationale: The quant model flags a Sell on the 1-year axis, driven by weak recent growth/momentum during a period when a crippling 50% US tariff was in effect. That tariff has since been cut to 18% (effective Feb 2026) — a major, dated, verifiable de-risking event — and FY26 results already show revenue and profit growth resuming with margin expansion. Per the asymmetric-override rule, I am rescuing this quant Sell to Hold on the strength of this concrete, forward-relevant catalyst; this is not a discretionary upgrade but a correction for information the trailing-data-driven quant score could not yet reflect.
summary: Avanti Feeds is India's largest shrimp-feed and processing company, whose stock and recent growth suffered under a severe 50% US tariff on Indian shrimp exports. That tariff was cut to 18% in February 2026, materially improving the competitive and earnings outlook, and FY26 results already show revenue and profit growth resuming with expanding margins. We are upgrading the quant model's Sell signal to a Hold given this concrete, dated de-risking catalyst.
positive_para: The US tariff cut from 50% to 18% (effective February 2026), together with new EU and UK trade agreements, materially improves Indian shrimp exporters' competitive position versus Ecuador and other rivals, and FY26 results already show this translating into resumed revenue growth (+8.3%), processed-shrimp export growth (+20%), and margin expansion (operating margin to 12%) — a genuine recovery in train, not just a hoped-for one.
negative_para: The shrimp aquaculture and export business remains inherently volatile — subject to disease outbreaks affecting farmer offtake, feed-cost inflation, and further shifts in US trade policy that could reverse some of the recent tariff relief — and even at 18%, the US tariff remains higher than competing origins, so Indian shrimp has not fully regained its prior cost competitiveness, only partially recovered it; growth here should be read as a normalization off a depressed base, not a new structural acceleration.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a PE of ~23x, the market is pricing in a moderate recovery, consistent with what the tariff cut and FY26 results actually support; this is neither a distressed valuation demanding a Sell nor a rich one demanding caution — it looks like a fair price for a normalizing, still cyclically volatile export business.
